events.title: Saturn at Opposition
events.description: Saturn is closest to Earth. Rings are beautifully tilted for viewing.
events.how_to_observe: Visible all night. Even a small telescope reveals Saturn's rings clearly.

events.title: June Solstice - Longest Day
events.description: Summer solstice. The longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.
events.how_to_observe: Notice the Sun at its highest arc across the sky.

events.title: Mars at Opposition
events.description: Mars is closest to Earth. Surface details visible in telescopes.
events.how_to_observe: Rises at sunset, visible all night. Telescopes reveal polar ice caps.

events.title: Perseids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to 100 meteors per hour. The most popular meteor shower of the year.
events.how_to_observe: Best midnight to dawn. Look northeast. Warm summer nights - ideal viewing.

events.title: Partial Solar Eclipse
events.description: Partial solar eclipse visible from northern Europe, northern Asia, North America.
events.how_to_observe: Use certified solar eclipse glasses. NEVER look directly at the Sun.

events.title: Total Lunar Eclipse - Second Blood Moon
events.description: Total lunar eclipse visible from Americas, Europe, Africa, Middle East.
events.how_to_observe: Best viewed in dark skies. Red color most vivid 10+ minutes into totality.

events.title: Mercury at Greatest Elongation
events.description: Mercury at its highest above the horizon after sunset.
events.how_to_observe: Look west-northwest just after sunset. Low on horizon - needs clear view.

events.title: September Equinox - Fall Begins
events.description: Autumnal equinox. Day and night nearly equal. Fall begins.

events.title: Comet C/2025 PANSTARRS
events.description: Comet may become visible to the naked eye. Predicted magnitude 4-5.
events.how_to_observe: Best in dark skies away from city lights. Binoculars recommended.

events.title: Orionids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to 20 meteors per hour. Debris from Halley's Comet.

events.title: Leonids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to 15 meteors per hour. Known for occasional meteor storms.
events.how_to_observe: Best in early morning. Look east.

events.title: Geminids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to 150 meteors per hour. The year's best meteor shower.
events.how_to_observe: Best from 10 PM onwards. Look east. Bright, slow-moving meteors.

events.title: December Solstice - Shortest Day
events.description: Winter solstice. The shortest day and longest night of the year.
events.how_to_observe: Notice the Sun at its lowest arc across the sky.

events.title: Great Conjunction - Jupiter & Saturn
events.description: Jupiter and Saturn in extremely close approach. A rare 'double planet' visible to the naked eye.
events.how_to_observe: Look southwest after sunset. Visible as two bright planets very close together.
